cards.target: Beth yw enw'r ci?
cards.english: What's the dog's name?

cards.target: Dyna beth yw caredigrwydd.
cards.english: That's what kindness is.

cards.target: Beth yw'ch cymwysterau chi?
cards.english: What are your qualifications?

cards.target: Beth yw'ch barn chi?
cards.english: What is your opinion? (formal)

cards.target: Pam na ddest ti?
cards.english: Why didn't you come? (informal)
cards.existing: Comparatives: `yn fwy` (bigger), `yn llai` (smaller), `yn well` (better), `yn waeth` (worse). Use `na`/`nag` for 'than'.

cards.target: Beth yw'r eitem nesaf?
cards.english: What is the next item?

cards.target: Pryd mae dy ben-blwydd di?
cards.english: When is your birthday?

cards.target: Ydych chi'n derbyn arian parod?
cards.english: Do you accept cash?

cards.target: Mae'r athro'n gosod gwaith cartref.
cards.english: The teacher sets homework.

cards.target: Does dim bara ar ôl.
cards.english: There's no bread left.
cards.existing: `Does dim` = 'there isn't / there's no'. `Does dim coffi` (there's no coffee). Negation of existence – different from negating an action.

cards.target: Ydych chi'n rhydd nos Sadwrn?
cards.english: Are you free Saturday night?

cards.target: Beth mae dy rieni'n wneud?
cards.english: What do your parents do?

cards.target: Dw i eisiau'r un glas.
cards.english: I want the blue one.
cards.existing: `Eisiau` is the major exception to the `yn`-rule. Even though `dw i eisiau` looks like it should have `'n`, it doesn't – `eisiau` is special.

cards.target: Mae'r fferi'n cymryd tair awr.
cards.english: The ferry takes three hours.

cards.target: Un ferch a dau fachgen.
cards.english: One girl and two boys.
cards.existing: Welsh changes the start of a word in many cases. cath → fy nghath (my cat) → ei gath (his cat). Three patterns: soft, nasal, aspirate.

cards.target: Does dim tocynnau ar ôl.
cards.english: There are no tickets left.
cards.existing: `Does dim` = 'there isn't / there's no'. `Does dim coffi` (there's no coffee). Negation of existence – different from negating an action.

cards.target: Ble awn ni'r haf nesaf?
cards.english: Where will we go next summer?

cards.target: Ble alla i barcio'r car?
cards.english: Where can I park the car?

cards.target: Mae'r caffi gyferbyn â'r orsaf.
cards.english: The café is opposite the station.

cards.target: Mae'r farchnad rownd y gornel.
cards.english: The market is around the corner.

cards.target: Dw i'n magu tri o blant.
cards.english: I'm raising three children.

cards.target: Beth ydy ystyr y gair hwn?
cards.english: What does this word mean?

cards.target: Ydy hi'n mynd i fwrw glaw?
cards.english: Is it going to rain?

cards.target: Mae bwyd Cymreig yn ennill gwobrau.
cards.english: Welsh food is winning prizes.

cards.target: Mae hi'n gallu siarad tair iaith.
cards.english: She can speak three languages.

cards.target: Pwy sy'n gallu dod nos Wener?
cards.english: Who can come on Friday night?

cards.target: Mae'r bws yn dod bob ugain munud.
cards.english: The bus comes every twenty minutes.

cards.target: Mae'r trên yn gadael mewn deng munud.
cards.english: The train leaves in ten minutes.

cards.target: Does dim arian ar ôl gyda fi.
cards.english: I don't have any money left.
cards.existing: Past form: `Doedd dim` (there wasn't). Future: `Fydd dim` (there won't be). Each tense has its own existential negation form.

cards.target: Cymerwch yr ail dro ar y dde.
cards.english: Take the second turn on the right.
cards.existing: Singular/informal imperative drops the ending or uses the bare stem: `Eistedd!`, `Cymer!`, `Edrych!`. Compare to plural/formal `-wch`.

cards.target: Dydyn ni ddim wedi penderfynu ble i fynd.
cards.english: We haven't decided where to go.

cards.target: Dyw hi ddim yn gwybod am y newid.
cards.english: She doesn't know about the change.
cards.existing: `Ddim` is a soft mutation of `dim` (nothing/none). It does the negation work. Order: verb + subject + ddim + rest.

cards.target: Dw i ddim yn llwglyd ar hyn o bryd.
cards.english: I'm not hungry right now.

cards.target: Paid â gadael i un diwrnod gwael dy ddigalonni.
cards.english: Don't let one bad day discourage you.

cards.target: Dal ati i ofyn cwestiynau, dyna sut rwyt ti'n dysgu.
cards.english: Keep asking questions, that's how you learn.

cards.target: Disgwylir i'r tywydd wella.
cards.english: The weather is expected to improve.
cards.existing: `'r` is the contracted definite article – happens after a vowel: `mae'r ci` (the dog is). Sticks to the preceding vowel.

cards.target: Beth am damaid o gaws?
cards.english: How about a bit of cheese?

cards.target: Pryd wyt ti'n dod nôl?
cards.english: When are you coming back? (informal)

cards.target: Beth ydy'r gair Cymraeg am 'dog'?
cards.english: What is the Welsh word for 'dog'?

cards.target: Pryd mae'r fferi nesaf i Iwerddon?
cards.english: When is the next ferry to Ireland?

cards.target: O ble dych chi'n dod yn wreiddiol?
cards.english: Where are you originally from?
cards.existing: Plural forms of present `bod`: `dyn ni'n` / `rydym ni'n` (we are), `dych chi'n` / `rydych chi'n` (you all are).

cards.target: Mae e'n gryfach nag y mae'n edrych.
cards.english: He is stronger than he looks.

cards.target: Mae angen swyddi yn yr ardaloedd gwledig.
cards.english: Jobs are needed in rural areas.

cards.target: Mae pennaeth newydd yn ein hysgol ni.
cards.english: Our school has a new headteacher.

cards.target: Dyw hi ddim yn meindio'r tywydd oer.
cards.english: She doesn't mind the cold weather.

cards.target: Does dim signal ffôn yn y cwm.
cards.english: There is no phone signal in the valley.
cards.existing: Past form: `Doedd dim` (there wasn't). Future: `Fydd dim` (there won't be). Each tense has its own existential negation form.

cards.target: Mae'r Mabinogi'n un o drysorau llenyddiaeth Gymraeg.
cards.english: The Mabinogi is one of the treasures of Welsh literature.

cards.target: Dw i'n cael brecwast am saith o'r gloch.
cards.english: I have breakfast at seven o'clock.

cards.target: Dw i ddim yn dda iawn am goginio.
cards.english: I'm not very good at cooking.
cards.existing: `Ddim` is a soft mutation of `dim` (nothing/none). It does the negation work. Order: verb + subject + ddim + rest.

cards.target: Mae'r ŵyl fwyd yn denu miloedd o ymwelwyr.
cards.english: The food festival attracts thousands of visitors.

cards.target: Mae e'n cerdded yn arafach ers y llawdriniaeth.
cards.english: He walks more slowly since the operation.

cards.target: Sut dw i'n mynd i ganol y dref?
cards.english: How do I get to the town centre?

cards.target: A bod yn onest, mae'r sefyllfa'n gymhleth iawn.
cards.english: To be honest, the situation is very complex.
cards.existing: `A` at sentence start (in questions, before verb) = question particle. Often dropped in spoken Welsh: `(A) wyt ti'n dod?`.

cards.target: Dyn ni'n treulio'r Nadolig gyda'r teulu bob blwyddyn.
cards.english: We spend Christmas with the family every year.

cards.target: Mae'r athro yn marcio'r arholiadau dros y penwythnos.
cards.english: The teacher marks the exams over the weekend.

cards.target: Mae'r Gymraeg yn un o'r ieithoedd Celtaidd hynaf.
cards.english: Welsh is one of the oldest Celtic languages.
cards.existing: Welsh numbers 1-10 have masculine and feminine forms: `dau/dwy` (2), `tri/tair` (3), `pedwar/pedair` (4). Match the noun's gender.

cards.target: Mae'r hediad yn cymryd awr a deugain munud.
cards.english: The flight takes an hour and forty minutes.

cards.target: Y trên dw i'n ddal, nid y bws.
cards.english: It's the train I catch, not the bus.

cards.target: Beth dych chi'n hoffi wneud ar y penwythnos?
cards.english: What do you like to do at the weekend?

cards.target: Ble gallaf i barcio fy nghar yn y dref?
cards.english: Where can I park my car in town?

cards.target: Pryd mae Dewi'n gorffen gwaith ac yn dod adref?
cards.english: When does Dewi finish work and come home?

cards.target: Mae hi wedi ysgrifennu dau lyfr am hanes Cymru.
cards.english: She has written two books about Welsh history.
cards.existing: Slot system: Dw i'n bwyta (present) → Dw i wedi bwyta (perfect) → Dw i'n mynd i fwyta (future). The middle word switches the tense.

cards.target: Mae'n braf cwrdd â chi am y tro cyntaf.
cards.english: It's nice to meet you for the first time.

cards.target: Mae gen i ddau o blant, bachgen a merch.
cards.english: I have two children, a boy and a girl.

cards.target: Mae'r Gymraeg yn un o'r ieithoedd hynaf yn Ewrop.
cards.english: Welsh is one of the oldest languages in Europe.
cards.existing: Numbers trigger mutations: `dau gi` (two dogs – soft), `tri chi` (three dogs – aspirate). Different number, different mutation.

cards.target: Faint o amser mae'n cymryd i gerdded i'r copa?
cards.english: How long does it take to walk to the summit?

cards.target: Faint o amser mae'n ei gymryd i yrru i Lundain?
cards.english: How long does it take to drive to London?

cards.target: Mae'r trên i Gaerdydd yn gadael am hanner awr wedi deg.
cards.english: The train to Cardiff leaves at half past ten.

cards.target: Dw i ddim yn bwyta cig, oes bwyd llysieuol gyda chi?
cards.english: I don't eat meat, do you have vegetarian food?

cards.target: Mae cyfryngau cymdeithasol yn dylanwadu ar sut mae pobl ifanc yn cyfathrebu.
cards.english: Social media influences how young people communicate.

cards.target: Mae gan Peredur ddau dŷ, un yn y dref ac un yn y wlad.
cards.english: Peredur has two houses, one in town and one in the country.

cards.target: Mae'r cynhwysydd yn storio ynni trydanol.
cards.english: The capacitor stores electrical energy.

cards.target: Mae'r argraffydd tri dimensiwn yn creu cydrannau metel.
cards.english: The 3D printer creates metal components.

cards.target: Mae'r dryw yn un o adar lleiaf Prydain.
cards.english: The wren is one of Britain's smallest birds.
cards.existing: Modern decimal counting (1, 2, ... 10, 11, 12 ...) is common in everyday speech, but the traditional vigesimal system (counts by 20) still appears, especially for dates and time.

cards.target: Mae'r amffitheatr Rhufeinig yn dyddio o'r ail ganrif.
cards.english: The Roman amphitheatre dates from the second century.

cards.target: Mae'r tatws pum munud yn bryd cyflym a maethlon.
cards.english: Five-minute potatoes are a quick and nutritious dish.

cards.target: Mae masnach deg yn sicrhau bod cynhyrchwyr yn cael pris teg.
cards.english: Fair trade ensures producers receive a fair price.
